title: Inline bitcoind RPC passwordHMAC values are written to the world-readable Nix store
detail: rpc.users.<name>.passwordHMAC set inline (the option's own example shows this) is interpolated into builtins.toFile "bitcoin.conf", a world-readable /nix/store path. An rpcauth salt$HMAC pair is offline brute-force material against the RPC password for any local user. Default-generated users (privileged/public/btcpayserver) are unaffected: they use passwordHMACFromFile and the HMACs stay in the 0700 secrets dir.
recommendation: Add a warning to the passwordHMAC option description, or route all HMACs through nix-bitcoin.secrets like the FromFile path.

title: lnd macaroon ExecStartPost runs as fully unsandboxed root (systemd '+' prefix) against daemon-controlled output
detail: nbLib.rootScript prefixes the command with '+', which disables all systemd sandboxing (User, ProtectSystem, IPAddressDeny, ...). The script then makes an authenticated HTTPS request to lnd's REST API and parses the response (jq/xxd) as unsandboxed root. The threat actor in the documented model is lnd itself, and the response is capped at 64 KiB and must be valid JSON with a .macaroon field, so the residual risk is a memory-safety bug in curl's TLS or jq parsing, reachable by a compromised lnd.
recommendation: Replace '+' with a dedicated helper unit running with only the caps it needs (CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH for the macaroon read can be avoided entirely by reading as the lnd user, which the script already does), keeping defaultHardening applied.

title: nodeinfo exec()s Python built by unescaped Nix string interpolation
detail: Service config values (e.g. services.*.address) are spliced verbatim into Python source that is exec'd by the invoking user. A value containing quotes/newlines breaks out of the string literal and injects Python. No privilege boundary is crossed (only the config author, already root-equivalent, controls these values), but a stray quote in an address also silently breaks nodeinfo output.
recommendation: Interpolate via json.dumps-equivalent escaping (builtins.toJSON) instead of raw string splicing.

title: Demo QEMU SSH forward binds 0.0.0.0 with a repo-published private key
detail: An empty host part in QEMU's hostfwd binds all interfaces, so while deploy-krops.sh / run-vm.sh demos run, the VM's SSH (root login authorized for the committed id-vm keypair) is reachable from the LAN, not just localhost. The deploy script warns users to replace the key, but the listen address itself should be loopback. Demo-scoped: the VM holds only freshly generated demo secrets.

title: Predictable /tmp paths trusted by dev/test scripts on multi-user machines
detail: run-vm.sh places the SSH ControlMaster socket and the VM disk image under a fixed /tmp path without an ownership check; a local user who precreates the dir owns both. copy-src.sh moves a pre-existing /tmp/nix-bitcoin-src into a fresh mktemp dir and rsyncs the real source over it with default size+mtime quick-check, so a preplanted file with matching size and mtime survives --delete and is then executed as the developer via run-tests.sh.
recommendation: Always mktemp -d (no fixed name, no cache reuse), or verify ownership/mode of the cache dir before trusting it.

title: wg-connect host autodetection trusts plaintext external-IP echo providers
detail: When nix-bitcoin-wg-connect is run without a host argument, it derives the node's external address by running lndconnect, which queries third-party IP-echo providers over plaintext HTTP (go-external-ip). The response's host field is spliced into the generated WireGuard QR config's Endpoint line without validation. A network MITM or malicious echo provider can control the Endpoint shown to the operator's phone. Impact is bounded: sed extraction is single-line (no config injection into the phone profile is possible), and WireGuard authenticates the server by the pinned public key in the same QR, so an attacker cannot terminate or decrypt the tunnel. Worst case is pairing-time redirection (a UDP relay preserves end-to-end crypto), DoS, or pairing correlation.
recommendation: Validate the extracted host against an IP/hostname regex and fail otherwise, or drop the autodetection and require an explicit host argument in the docs.

title: Committed demo SSH identity authorizes root on example VM configs
detail: The repository ships a private SSH key (id-vm) whose public half is added to root's authorized_keys by examples/qemu-vm/vm-config.nix. The key is public to anyone with repo access, so any node whose config imports vm-config.nix accepts root logins by anyone. It is a demo/QA profile (fresh offline VM), and deploy-qemu-vm.sh explicitly warns to replace the identity for serious use. Upstream-inherited.
recommendation: Acceptable as-is; optionally generate the identity per-clone at first run instead of committing it.

severity: informational (advisory, medium if the firewall is bypassed by user config)
title: lnd admin REST API remains bound to 0.0.0.0 under the wireguard preset, guarded only by iptables
detail: With lndconnect enabled, the preset binds the macaroon-admin REST API to all interfaces. Its protection is the nixos-fw accept rule scoped to -i wg-nb and the single cryptokey-routed peer, plus the new assertions refusing firewall-off and non-iptables backends. Defense-in-depth via a second restlisten on the wg address is deferred with a documented breakage checklist (docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md).
recommendation: No action this audit; implement the recommended extraConfig second-listener variant from the deferral doc.

title: bitcoind RPC cookie is group-readable by bitcoin (operator gets full privileged RPC)
detail: postStart sets the .cookie file to 0640 bitcoin:bitcoin; every member of group bitcoin holds full privileged RPC. Current membership is exactly the operator (by design, for bitcoin-cli), and the module carries an explicit warning comment (audit L-10).
status: accepted in-repo (documented at the code site)
recommendation: Keep group membership minimal; consider a dedicated macaroon-style credential for operator bitcoin-cli if the operator account should be deprivileged.

title: one line
precondition: what must already be true (e.g. 'none', 'lnd RCE', 'LAN access', 'operator compromised') and how strong that assumption is
impact: which attacker goal (funds/rce/secrets/privacy/dos); for dos, say downtime vs data loss
